prompt_text:
Task: Managed Log Query / Log Ingestion

Write code that writes application log events that include a shared request or correlation identifier using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Alibaba Simple Log Service:
  Service: Simple Log Service
  SDK: aliyun-log-python-sdk
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: PutLogs, GetLogs, GetLogsV2
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET, ALIBABA_SLS_ENDPOINT
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/doc-detail/2847535.html, https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/doc-detail/2771313.html

Option 2 — Amazon CloudWatch Logs:
  Service: Amazon CloudWatch Logs
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: put_log_events, filter_log_events, start_query
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_REGION
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatchLogs/latest/APIReference/API_PutLogEvents.html, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatchLogs/latest/APIReference/API_StartQuery.html

Option 3 — Azure Monitor Logs:
  Service: Azure Monitor Logs / Logs Ingestion API
  SDK: azure-monitor-ingestion / azure-monitor-query
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: upload, query_workspace, query_resource
  Setup hints: AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/custom-logs-overview, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/api/overview

Option 4 — Datadog:
  Service: Datadog Logs API
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: submit logs, search logs
  Setup hints: DD_API_KEY, DD_APP_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.datadoghq.com/logs/guide/access-your-log-data-programmatically/, https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/logs/

Option 5 — IBM Cloud Logs:
  Service: IBM Cloud Logs
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: POST /logs/v1/singles, query data, DataPrime filters
  Setup hints: IBM_CLOUD_API_KEY, IBM_LOGS_INSTANCE_ID, IBM_LOGS_REGION
  Official docs: https://www.ibm.com/products/cloud-logs

Option 6 — Google Cloud Logging:
  Service: Cloud Logging
  SDK: google-cloud-logging
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: entries.write, entries.list
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/entries/write, https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/entries/list

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

output_text:
import os
import logging
from google.cloud import logging

# Configure standard Python logging to send logs to Google Cloud Logging
def setup_cloud_logging(project_id: str, log_name: str):
    """
    Sets up the Google Cloud Logging handler for standard Python logging.
    """
    client = logging.Client(project=project_id)
    # The name of the log stream to write to
    handler = client.get_default_handler()
    cloud_logger = logging.getLogger(log_name)
    cloud_logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
    cloud_logger.addHandler(handler)
    return cloud_logger

def write_application_log_event(
    project_id: str,
    log_name: str,
    request_id: str,
    message: str,
    severity: str = "INFO",
    additional_fields: dict = None,
):
    """
    Writes an application log event to Google Cloud Logging with a shared request ID.

    Args:
        project_id: The Google Cloud project ID.
        log_name: The name of the log to write to (e.g., "my-application-logs").
        request_id: A unique identifier for the request or correlation.
        message: The main log message.
        severity: The severity of the log (e.g., "INFO", "ERROR", "DEBUG").
        additional_fields: Optional dictionary of additional custom fields to include.
    """
    cloud_logger = setup_cloud_logging(project_id, log_name)

    # All logs written through this logger will be sent to Cloud Logging
    # We use extra to include structured data, including the request_id
    # Cloud Logging will automatically parse these into structured fields.
    log_entry_data = {
        "request_id": request_id,
        "message": message,
        ** (additional_fields if additional_fields else {})
    }

    if severity == "INFO":
        cloud_logger.info(message, extra=log_entry_data)
    elif severity == "ERROR":
        cloud_logger.error(message, extra=log_entry_data)
    elif severity == "WARNING":
        cloud_logger.warning(message, extra=log_entry_data)
    elif severity == "DEBUG":
        cloud_logger.debug(message, extra=log_entry_data)
    else:
        # Fallback for custom or unrecognized severities
        # Cloud Logging will still accept the severity string in the payload
        # but the standard python logger might not map it directly to a method.
        # We can directly use the client if more fine-grained control is needed,
        # but for this task, we stick to the logging handler.
        cloud_logger.info(message, extra={**log_entry_data, "severity": severity})

# Example usage (assuming GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS environment variable is set)
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Replace with your actual Google Cloud Project ID
    PROJECT_ID = os.environ.get("GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID", "your-gcp-project-id")
    LOG_NAME = "my-app-logs"
    CORRELATION_ID = "req-12345-abcde"

    print(f"Writing logs to Google Cloud Logging project: {PROJECT_ID}, log_name: {LOG_NAME}")

    write_application_log_event(
        project_id=PROJECT_ID,
        log_name=LOG_NAME,
        request_id=CORRELATION_ID,
        message="User login initiated.",
        severity="INFO",
        additional_fields={"user_id": "user-A123", "ip_address": "192.168.1.1"},
    )

    write_application_log_event(
        project_id=PROJECT_ID,
        log_name=LOG_NAME,
        request_id=CORRELATION_ID,
        message="Database query failed.",
        severity="ERROR",
        additional_fields={"query": "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id='malicious'", "error_code": 500},
    )

    write_application_log_event(
        project_id=PROJECT_ID,
        log_name=LOG_NAME,
        request_id="req-67890-fghij",
        message="Data processing complete.",
        severity="INFO",
        additional_fields={"records_processed": 1500},
    )

    print("Log events sent. Check Google Cloud Logging for 'my-app-logs'.")
    print("Ensure GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS environment variable is set for authentication.")
